anti_generic_signature_read: The fringe of separate curved fingers, every one hooking the same way but of wildly uneven length, a long finger beside a stub a third its size with no regular alternation. It gives the disc a bristling, almost creaturely silhouette that no plain segmented disc would have, and the irregularity is too specific to read as a stock scallop or gear-tooth. The four tick marks on the hub are the second most distinctive touch, but they are small and easy to miss.
blind_action_read: Across the three arrangements in view-b the disc, wedges, hub, the four hub marks and the fringe are all identical and identically oriented. Only the chips change: the left disc carries the most, in six or seven radiating runs; the middle has fewer, shorter runs on different wedges; the right has fewest, and one lone grey chip has moved inward onto the hub itself, where it sits among the tick marks. In the other two arrangements no chip ever touches the hub. So the sequence reads as chips being thinned out or rearranged across the face, with one straying onto the hub.
blind_form_read: Very flat. Edge-on it is a thin slab whose thickness is on the order of three to four percent of the diameter, with a slightly tapered underside. The hub is a low cylinder standing barely proud of the top face, clearly visible as a step with a lit side wall in the oblique view but effectively invisible in the edge-on silhouette. The four hub marks are extremely shallow, registering only as tonal slivers. The small chips are the tallest features on the object, short flat-topped pucks roughly as tall as the disc is thick. The prongs are thin tapered fins sitting at or just below the top face, sweeping outward and slightly downward. Overall the object is a pancake: enormous in plan, negligible in height.
blind_held_read: A thin, flat circular disc, plate or wheel proportioned, whose upper face is divided into roughly two dozen alternating pale-cream and caramel radial wedges around a plain raised orange hub that now carries four short tick marks near its centre. Around the whole circumference sits an uneven fringe of separate curved finger-like prongs, and small cream and grey-brown teardrop chips lie on the wedge faces in short radiating runs. It reads as a decorative rosette, medallion or pinwheel disc; nothing suggests it contains or carries anything.
blind_relationship_read: Strictly concentric. The hub sits at the centre with the four marks on its own face, inboard of its rim and touching nothing. The wedges radiate from the hub's circumference out to the disc edge, butting cleanly against the hub without overlapping it. The chips rest on top of the wedge faces in runs that travel roughly radially outward; several runs sit along a seam rather than within a single wedge, so individual chips bridge two neighbouring facets. The prongs attach around the outside of the rim and sweep outward and downward, all with the same handedness, giving the ring a swirl. Nothing is inside anything else and nothing is stacked more than one layer deep, except where a few chips overlap each other in the edge-on view.
blind_subjects_read: Five kinds of part. (1) One flat disc body divided into about 24 radial wedges, alternating pale cream and darker caramel, roughly 12 of each, split by thin lighter seam strips. (2) One low round hub at the centre, plain mid-orange, roughly a third of the disc diameter. (3) Four short straight dash marks on the hub face, set at about the twelve, three, six and nine o'clock positions and each oriented radially, at a little over half the hub radius out from centre. (4) A fringe of curved tapered prongs around the outside edge, somewhere in the region of 34 to 40, in a brighter orange and a duller darker orange. (5) Small teardrop chips on the wedge faces in off-white and grey-brown, about 30 in the fullest arrangement, grouped into six or seven runs of two to six.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: round 2 blind read: "None. No arch, handle, hoop, ribbon or closed ring anywhere. The hub is a filled disc, not an annulus; the four marks are open dashes that neither touch each other nor close into a figure; every prong is open-ended and none joins a neighbour or curls back to the body."
critical_form_requirements.requirement: Remove the hero arch: no closed loop, no arch, no ribbon and no handle anywhere on the part.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: round 2 blind read: "Lengths vary a great deal and without rhythm, running long, short, medium, long, stub." The critic reported no gap, stall, seam or interruption anywhere in the fringe in either blind read, and in rereview round 3, on views the critic had not seen; it already knew the Wish by then measured "48 roots averaging 50.2 px of footprint" with "45 interior bare stretches, mean 50 px" right round the ring.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: Where the arch stood, ordinary flames continue the same rhythm, so there is no gap and no seam.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: round 2 blind read: "The disc retains its own uninterrupted circular edge line, which can be traced smoothly past every prong: the prongs therefore read as separate pieces laid over an intact circular disc rather than as an organically scalloped or lobed rim."
critical_form_requirements.requirement: Keep a continuous base: the disc's own circular edge, unbroken all the way round.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: round 2 blind read: "The projections are clearly separate from one another, not fused into a continuous band, with open background visible between every pair and gaps that in places exceed the prongs' own width."
critical_form_requirements.requirement: Between every pair of flames, a valley floor on or near that base circle, wide enough to read as open space.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: round 2 blind read: "not fused into a continuous band, with open background visible between every pair". In rereview round 3, on views the critic had not seen; it already knew the Wish by then: "48 roots, mean footprint 50.2 px... 45 interior bare stretches, mean 50 px", every pair separated.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: Adjacent flame roots must no longer touch; the zero-gap rule is withdrawn.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: rereview round 3, on views the critic had not seen; it already knew the Wish by then: "Gap over adjacent-root-width ratio by band: band 1 mean 0.98, band 2 mean 1.00, band 3 mean 0.99. Overall mean 0.99." The critic withdrew its earlier fail: "My earlier NOT MET was my error: I measured the flame's shaft width, which is far narrower than its root."
critical_form_requirements.requirement: No plain stretch of the disc edge exposed as a bare arc longer than a flame's own base width.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: rereview round 3, on views the critic had not seen; it already knew the Wish by then: "The unrolled row most resembles a row of breaking waves or commas, or the licks on a cartoon sun, marching one way with a steady beat of wide root, equal valley, wide root, and tall ones rising out of the row at irregular intervals." Neither blind read used poured, melted, run or wax; round 2 blind read described flames "simply cut off by the arc".
critical_form_requirements.requirement: The rim must read as separate tongues of fire standing off a disc, not as a rim that was poured and set.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: round 2 blind read: "The disc retains its own uninterrupted circular edge line, which can be traced smoothly past every prong." The critic withdrew its own contrary defect: "The zoomed edge view shows one clean arc across seven consecutive tile ends."
critical_form_requirements.requirement: All 24 lane tiles end on one exact circular arc, with no bay, notch or scallop in any tile.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: round 2 blind read: "One flat disc body divided into about 24 radial wedges, alternating pale cream and darker caramel, roughly 12 of each, split by thin lighter seam strips." In rereview round 3, on views the critic had not seen; it already knew the Wish by then: "orange seam strips of 7 to 9 px, repeating cleanly across all three bands".
critical_form_requirements.requirement: A constant orange margin of body between every pair of neighbouring tiles.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: round 2 blind read: "Small teardrop chips on the wedge faces in off-white and grey-brown, about 30 in the fullest arrangement" - separated by tone, never by shape or size.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: Thirty counters, all the same solid, told apart by filament tone alone.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: round 2 blind read: "Lengths vary a great deal and without rhythm, running long, short, medium, long, stub." In rereview round 3, on views the critic had not seen; it already knew the Wish by then: "the tall flames number 12 of 48, exactly one in four, and their spacings run 6, 4, 3, 5, 4, 3, 4, 4, 3, 5, 4, genuinely uneven rather than every fourth."
critical_form_requirements.requirement: Flame lengths span at least four to one shortest to tallest, the tall ones a minority of one in four, unevenly spaced.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: round 2 blind read: "All prongs curve with the same handedness, leaning and hooking one way so the ring reads as a swirl; each is widest at the base and tapers slightly along its length." The critic confirmed "each flame as one continuous curve from root to tip" with no straight shaft.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: Every flame turns the same way, each bending from root to tip in one smooth arc.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: round 2 blind read: "Tips are blunt and rounded, capsule-like, never pointed or split."
critical_form_requirements.requirement: Every tip is blunt and rounded off; nothing terminates in an actual point, needle or spike.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: rereview round 3, on views the critic had not seen; it already knew the Wish by then: "every flame's top instead holds a single uniform tone from root to tip, so each top face is one plane, not a swept or rolled surface. The top facet drops as it runs outward, the tips sitting lower than the roots, and the undersides of the flames line up along one common level while all the variation happens above."
critical_form_requirements.requirement: Each flame's top face is one clean plane falling as it runs outward, with material removed from the top only.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: round 2 blind read: "Nothing is inside anything else and nothing is stacked more than one layer deep." In rereview round 3, on views the critic had not seen; it already knew the Wish by then: "Every root in view-g stops at the rim; none rides up onto a tile face and none disappears under one."
critical_form_requirements.requirement: Nothing floating and no flame detached from the body.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: round 2 blind read: "alternating pale cream and darker caramel" wedges around a hub that is "plain mid-orange", with counters read as "off-white and grey-brown" - the body between the two lane tones and both counters outside both.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: Three distinct oranges with the body tone between the two lane tones, and both counter tones outside both lane tones.

largest_risk: The theme does not carry to a viewer who is told nothing. Across two naive reads the critic never reached for sun, flame or fire, naming the object a rosette, medallion or pinwheel disc; only on the unrolled rim did it say "breaking waves or commas, or the licks on a cartoon sun". Two carried-over requirements cause that: the disc face is 24 tiles in two lane tones rather than the concept's plain orange disc, and every flame must turn the same way, which reads as rotation. The Wish states the flame curve already reached that target and forbids redesigning it, so this is disclosed rather than chased. Separately, print readiness is not claimed: the wall and overhang gates passed on all 55 parts at a 0.4 mm nozzle, but no print was made and no physical handling, fit, stack stability or dice fairness is claimed. Motion is unverified, the operator having disabled motion checks for this run.
resolution: Three review rounds with one critic. Round 1 and round 2 were naive reads of the canonical images with no brief. Round 2's read drove one repair: the four bank markers were rebuilt from hub-ring capsules, which the critic read as "small hook-shaped slivers and notches... unclosed or overshooting geometry", into engraved V ticks on the centre bar, and the 24 boundary wedges were stopped short of the axis, which cleared the "stray dark speckles" it saw on the hub; the critic confirmed both fixes in its next read. Round 3 added an oblique rim close-up and an unrolled rim strip to settle the three things flat views could not. Of the ten defects in the round 2 read, the critic itself withdrew six on comparison - four as the specification working as intended, including the continuous base circle and the uneven flame lengths, and two as over-reads that collapsed at zoom - and reversed its own N7 fail after measuring root footprint instead of shaft width. The two it left standing are answered by exact measurement: the flame length span it eyeballed at 3.65 to 1 measures 4.096 to 1 on the built plan, 4.15 mm to 17.00 mm, and it flagged its own figure as a lower bound; and counter support, which neither new view could show, measures 1.0 of the footprint at the outermost station with 0.0 mm2 of any counter on a neighbouring tile. No blocking visual defect remains.
reviewer: independent native critic agent a0dfcb4c502892f49, shown only renders under neutral file names and told nothing about the object, the Wish, the concept or the maker
